experiments.observed: A snapshot validated before transfer did not protect a later sequence-only append; the stale write was admitted. The atomic current-snapshot path rejected it.
The stale owner supplied the exact next sequence and was rejected with StaleOwnership; the current owner then used that sequence successfully.
The current owner supplied an already-used sequence and was independently rejected with LedgerSequenceMismatch.
Equal and lower transfer tokens were rejected with FenceRegression; a greater non-contiguous token was accepted.
A highest-seen sink accepted a distinct old-token write after authority transfer but before observing the new token, then rejected the old token after observing the new token.
An exact retry returned the prior entry without another write; changed content under the same operation identifier was rejected.

hypothesis.boundary: A token allocator or max-observed-token check alone is not sufficient. Every side-effect target must participate, current ownership and ledger position are distinct checks, validation must be atomic with the write, and the token high-water must not regress.
hypothesis.refuted_claim: A sink that remembers only its highest observed token does not reject every stale write immediately at ownership transfer; before the newer token arrives, an old equal token can still be accepted.
hypothesis.statement: Fencing tokens have known edge cases that should appear in fault fixtures.
